extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO processing/examining staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for inventor oaths/declarations, substitute statements, and correction or updating of inventorship (including in continuing, divisional, and provisional applications) under 37 CFR and MPEP guidance. Covers required contents, filing timing, forms, fees, authentication (foreign oaths), and Office processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor, or each individual who is a joint inventor of a claimed invention, in an application for patent (other than a provisional application) must execute an oath or declaration directed to the application, except as provided for in pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When joint inventors execute separate oaths or declarations, each oath or declaration should reference that the affiant is a joint inventor with the other named inventors (e.g., state original, first and joint inventor together with 'A' or 'A & B'). Forms PTO/SB/01 through PTO/SB/04 may be used for applications filed before September 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and bibliographic information in oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor’s oath or declaration must include certain inventor bibliographic information, name each inventor or joint inventor and, except as otherwise provided, be signed by each inventor, and identify the application to which it is directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 602.08(a)-(c) for details specific to inventor bibliographic information, required signature and name, and identification of the application. Unless included in an application data sheet (ADS), oaths and declarations must reference any foreign application for which priority is claimed (application number, country/office, and filing date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement availability and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement in compliance with 37 CFR 1.64 may be used when an inventor has not executed an oath/declaration, where permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute statements are only available for applications filed on or after September 16, 2012. Requirements for substitute statements are in 37 CFR 1.64 and MPEP § 604.

rubrics_metrics.name: New oath/declaration for continuation-in-part (CIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath or declaration must be filed in any continuation-in-part application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CIP may name all, more, or fewer inventors than the prior application; new matter in the CIP may necessitate a new oath or declaration. See 37 CFR 1.63(d)(1) and MPEP § 602.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying prior oath/declaration into continuing/divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of an oath or declaration from a prior application may be submitted with a continuation or divisional application, subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the copy is filed after the continuation/divisional filing date and an application number has been assigned, the cover letter should identify the new application number and indicate the copy is from a prior application to avoid incorrect file matching. Label the copy with the continuation/divisional application number in case the cover letter is separated from the copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration compliance when parent was filed pre-/post-September 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of a prior oath/declaration submitted to a continuing application filed on/after September 16, 2012 must comply with 35 U.S.C. 115 and 37 CFR 1.63 (or 1.64).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior application was filed before September 16, 2012, a new inventor’s oath or declaration may be required in the continuing application to meet post-2012 requirements (e.g., statement that the application was made or authorized to be made by the person executing the oath).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48 (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship in an application is permitted by amendment under 35 U.S.C. 116 and implemented by 37 CFR 1.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for correction may be submitted under the various 1.48 subsections depending on application type and timing; OPAP handles requests filed on/after September 16, 2012. 37 CFR 1.48 does not apply to reissue applications (see 37 CFR 1.171–1.175 and MPEP § 1412.04) and correction via certificate of correction uses different provisions (37 CFR 1.324).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(a) — Requirements for nonprovisional correction requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to correct or change inventorship once inventorship has been established must include (1) an application data sheet (ADS) identifying each inventor by legal name and (2) the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship is established upon the first submission of an ADS or an inventor’s oath/declaration. The ADS submitted with a 1.48(a) request must identify information being changed using underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for removals (per 37 CFR 1.76(c)(2)). 1.48(a) enables correction where improper inventorship was set forth or where prosecution leads to adding/deleting inventors (e.g., claims added or canceled).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(b) — Oath/declaration for added inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration as required by 37 CFR 1.63, or a substitute statement in compliance with 37 CFR 1.64, is required for any actual inventor who has not yet executed such an oath/declaration when added under 1.48(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after September 16, 2012 the oath must comply with post-2012 37 CFR 1.63; for prior-filed applications pre-AIA 1.63 applies. See MPEP § 602.01(b) and § 602.01(c)(1) for further details and references to 37 CFR 1.64 and MPEP § 604.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(c) — Fee when request filed after an office action on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: A request under 37 CFR 1.48 filed after the Office action on the merits has been given or mailed in the application must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(d), in addition to the processing fee, unless the request is due solely to cancellation of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventors are being deleted and the change is solely due to cancelation of claims, the additional fee need not be paid if accompanied by a statement to that effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(d) — Correction in provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For provisional applications, any request to correct or change inventorship must include (1) a request signed by a party set forth in 37 CFR 1.33(b) identifying each inventor by legal name and (2) the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding an inventor to a provisional, applicants should also file a corrected ADS or a new cover sheet providing the residence of all inventors (see 37 CFR 1.51(c)). Correction under 1.48(d) may not be necessary unless there would be no overlap of inventors upon filing the later nonprovisional; requests may still be filed after the twelve-month expiration with OPAP in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(f) — Correcting/updating inventor name or order
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to correct or update the name of an inventor or a joint inventor, or the order of the names of joint inventors, in a nonprovisional application must include (1) an ADS in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76 that identifies each inventor by legal name in desired order, and (2) the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted changes include legal name changes (e.g., marriage), typographical/transliteration errors, or reversing family/given names; the ADS must identify the information being changed as required by 1.76(c)(2). Applicant may also submit a new oath or declaration to correct earlier deficiencies (see 37 CFR 1.67(a) and MPEP § 601.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction by filing a continuing application (37 CFR 1.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship may be obtained by filing a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53 without filing a 37 CFR 1.48 request, provided the continuing application meets statutory requirements (e.g., inventorship overlap for 35 U.S.C. 120 benefit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 120 permits a continuing application to claim the benefit of a prior copending parent application if there is inventorship overlap between the continuing and parent applications; the overlap need not be present on the filing date of the continuing application or when the parent issues. However, refiling solely to change inventorship could cause loss of benefit if no overlap exists. Adding an inventor via 1.48 may result in loss of power of attorney if the added inventor does not provide a consistent power of attorney per 37 CFR 1.32(e). For continuing apps filed on/after Sep 16, 2012, inventorship is the inventors specified in the ADS filed before or with the copy of the prior oath/declaration; absent an ADS, inventorship is as in the copy of the prior oath unless accompanied by a 37 CFR 1.33(b) signed statement naming inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office processing of defective oaths or declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are not required to review inventor oaths/declarations; non-examiner staff reviews oaths/declarations for compliance and may send informational notices or requirements to correct deficiencies before or after allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an oath/declaration compliant with 37 CFR 1.63 or substitute under 1.64 has not been submitted by allowance, a Notice requiring the oath/declaration may be sent with the Notice of Allowability; the required oath or declaration must be submitted no later than the date the issue fee is paid (35 U.S.C. 115(f)). The Office does not check the date of execution or require new oaths based on 'staleness' (execution more than three months prior to filing) or omission of execution date, but wording should not be amended after signing. Some deficiencies can be corrected by supplemental papers (e.g., ADS or certificate from a notary). See MPEP § 602.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign executed oaths — authentication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath executed in a foreign country must be properly authenticated and may be made before specified authorized officials; the Office will accept foreign oaths if properly apostilled or authenticated as required by 37 CFR 1.66.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hague Convention apostilles are accepted for member countries (no diplomatic/consular certificate required). For non-member countries, the authority of the officer must be proved by certificate of a U.S. diplomatic or consular officer. If an oath taken in a foreign country is not properly authenticated, the application may still be accepted for examination but the applicant should submit a properly authenticated oath, an apostille, or a declaration under 37 CFR 1.68. The Office does not return improperly authenticated oaths for proper authentication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to recite foreign priority applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless included in an ADS, oaths and declarations must reference any foreign application for patent (or inventor’s certificate) for which priority is claimed, including foreign application number, country/office, and filing date of each foreign application to which priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63(c)(2) and MPEP § 602.03 for additional information. The applicant is required to recite all foreign applications filed prior to the application on which priority is claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and fee requirements and available forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific forms and fees are required for certain submissions: PTO/AIA/40 may be used to request correction of inventorship or name/order changes; forms PTO/SB/01–04 may be used for inventor’s oath/declaration in pre-Sep 16, 2012 applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing and additional fees referenced include 37 CFR 1.17(i) (processing fee for 1.48 requests), 1.17(d) (fee when filing after an office action on the merits), and 1.17(q) (provisional processing fee). Forms are available on the USPTO website (www.uspto.gov/PatentForms). The ADS and its formatting requirements (underlining/strike-through) are governed by 37 CFR 1.76.
